newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Disneyland operator shows good rise in debut.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Disneyland operator shows good rise in debut.

text.p: Tokyo Disneyland operator Oriental Land Co Ltd made a healthy gain in its debut on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Wednesday, but disappointed brokers said it did not appear to lure new money into the market.
Despite the cachet of the worldwide "Disney" brand, the issue was dogged by uncertainties about funding for Oriental Land's second theme park, due to open in 2001, brokers said.
"It is an issue with a promising future, but it doesn't seem to be attracting new money into the stock market for now," said Haruyoshi Mabuchi, chief strategist at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
Oriental Land operates Tokyo Disnelyand under a licensing agreement with Walt Disney Co.

Brokers also said some of the investors who bought shares of Oriental Land, the TSE's last major new issue for this year, did so by selling other shares, thus limiting the net gain for the market as a whole.
Oriental's share price opened at 8,850 yen ($78), slightly higher than expected, and briefly climbed to 9,030 yen ($79) before it was hit by profit taking, brokers said.

The stock ended its first day of trade at 8,800 yen ($77), far above the initial offer price of 8,050 yen ($71) set on November 27. With volume of 8.5 million shares, it was the most heavily traded stock today on the TSE's first section.
Analysts and investors expected Oriental Land shares to steer a steady course in the future, although they might encounter short-term profit taking.

"We'll have to wait and see how the price moves for a while, but after a round of short-term sales it would be good to pick up the shares for the long term," said Hitoshi Morimura, chief fund manager at Meiji Life Insurance Co.
He said that Oriental Land is likely to be supported by index-related buying, as the shares will be the leading issue in the entertainment sector.
Analysts also said that the future of Oriental Land, which earns 97 percent of its revenue from Tokyo Disneyland, hinges on the fate of a second planned theme park, "Tokyo Disney Sea."
Oriental Land has not unveiled details of the new park, although it is to be located next to Tokyo Disneyland and will be about the same scale.
Analysts said there were also concerns about financing the new park.

Oriental Land president Toshio Kagami said at a news conference that the company expects its profits to dip in the period between 1998/99 and 2001/2002 business years, due to investments in the second theme park.

Oriental Land announced on Wednesday that it sees parent current profits at 29.07 billion yen ($257 million) for the business year that ends on March 31, 1997. Its actual profit in the year through March 1996 was 28.08 billion yen ($248 million). ($=113 yen)
